title: Mathematics — Friday, 6 November 2026 arXiv announcement batch — 8 notable recent papers
global_caveat: arXiv publishes no official trending chart; this is an inferred ordering of notable recent work, not measured popularity, and citation evidence is limited for papers this recent.

sections.title: Resolving Tusnády's Problem
sections.abstract: For each fixed dimension d≥3, the authors prove an anchored-box discrepancy lower bound of order (log N)^(d−1/2), which together with known upper and planar lower bounds yields the sharp order for all fixed d≥2.
sections.claimed_result: The author proves Ω_d((log N)^(d−1/2)) for anchored boxes when fixed d≥3; with the cited matching upper bound and planar lower bound, this gives Θ_d((log N)^(d−1/2)) for axis-parallel boxes in every fixed d≥2 (arXiv abstract and Theorem 1.1).
sections.assumptions_and_setting: Worst-case combinatorial discrepancy of finite N-point sets in fixed-dimensional Euclidean space; constants may depend on dimension.
sections.unique_caveat: The new lower-bound proof is for d≥3; the two-dimensional lower bound and matching upper bound are prior results used to complete the stated conclusion.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: A concrete lower bound closes the dimension-at-least-three gap in a longstanding discrepancy problem; the result connects classical analysis, combinatorics, and computational geometry, and combines with cited upper and planar results.

sections.title: Tusnády's problem and online two-sample thinning
sections.abstract: The author obtains the sharp fixed-dimensional order for Tusnády discrepancy, a robust deletion lower bound, and minimax bounds for online thinning of two samples, including a sharp one-dimensional separation between prefix and terminal objectives.
sections.claimed_result: The author proves Θ_d((log N)^(d−1/2)) discrepancy for fixed d≥2; for online thinning with fixed k and expected deletion budget ρn, 0<ρ<2, minimax expected prefix discrepancy is Θ_(k,ρ)((log n)^(k+1/2)); for k=1, terminal discrepancy is Θ_ρ((log log n)^(3/2)).
sections.assumptions_and_setting: Two independent size-n samples from an unknown common distribution; observations must be kept or deleted on arrival, with fixed dimension and stated expected deletion budget. The discrepancy result is for fixed dimension and axis-parallel boxes.
sections.unique_caveat: For online terminal discrepancy in dimensions k≥2, the paper reports bounds still differing by a factor of log n.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: It combines the sharp discrepancy order with a high-probability robustness statement and a separate online sampling application; the cross-listing spans combinatorics, algorithms, and probability.

sections.title: On the critical value of void percolation in high dimensions
sections.abstract: For the random Lorentz gas, the authors prove that the void-percolation threshold grows linearly with dimension, with explicit sufficiently-large-dimension bounds between d/2 and 5d.
sections.claimed_result: The authors prove Φ_p(d)=Θ(d) and, for all sufficiently large d, d/2≤Φ_p(d)≤5d (arXiv abstract; introduction and main results).
sections.assumptions_and_setting: A point tracer moves among spherical obstacles centered on a Poisson point process in R^d; the threshold concerns loss of percolation of the vacant region as obstacle density increases.
sections.unique_caveat: The constants are not sharp and the bounds apply only for sufficiently large d; the exact leading coefficient is not determined.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: The theorem determines the scaling where prior bounds left even the order unresolved; probability and disordered-systems cross-listing reflects the mathematical-physics setting.

sections.title: Pointless K3 surfaces over finite fields
sections.abstract: The authors prove that a K3 surface with no rational point over F_q exists exactly when the finite-field size satisfies q≤11, using lattice bounds and the Artin–Tate formula.
sections.claimed_result: The authors prove that pointless K3 surfaces over F_q exist if and only if q≤11 (arXiv abstract and Theorem 1).
sections.assumptions_and_setting: Smooth K3 surfaces over finite fields, with q a prime power; pointless means having no F_q-rational points.
sections.unique_caveat: This classifies rational-point existence for K3 surfaces, not arbitrary varieties; the paper notes that the relationship between its lattice argument and another proof remains unexplored.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: A sharp if-and-only-if classification with a concrete boundary at q=11; the argument bridges arithmetic geometry and lattice optimization, and the authors note another proof of the same classification.

sections.title: Weak uniqueness for the stochastic heat equation with nondegenerate diffusion: the full Hölder regime
sections.abstract: For the scalar stochastic heat equation on the one-dimensional torus, the author proves weak well-posedness for uniformly nondegenerate diffusion coefficients of every positive Hölder order and gives extensions with measurable drift.
sections.claimed_result: For bounded uniformly nondegenerate Hölder diffusion, the author proves existence and uniqueness in law for the scalar equation at every positive Hölder exponent; a second theorem treats measurable drifts of linear growth under additional alternatives (arXiv abstract and Theorems 1.1–1.2).
sections.assumptions_and_setting: One-dimensional torus, scalar equation driven by space-time white noise, deterministic initial data in L² for the bounded-diffusion theorem, and diffusion bounded above and away from zero with positive Hölder regularity.
sections.unique_caveat: The theorem is weak uniqueness in this scalar model, not pathwise uniqueness; the unbounded-diffusion extension uses bounded initial data, a restriction the author identifies as a possible future relaxation.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: It resolves the stated weak-uniqueness question across the full positive Hölder range and includes an associated Lean formalization; it is a substantial probability result with an explicit stochastic-PDE setting.

sections.title: Exotic smooth structures on complex projective spaces
sections.abstract: The authors show that dimensions admitting exotic smooth structures on CP^n have natural density one and identify 266 residue classes modulo 288, covering over 92% of dimensions, where such structures exist for n>3.
sections.claimed_result: The authors prove density one of dimensions admitting an exotic smoothing and exhibit 266 congruence classes modulo 288, covering 266/288>92%, for which CP^n has an exotic smooth structure when n>3 (arXiv abstract and Theorems B–C).
sections.assumptions_and_setting: Smooth manifolds homeomorphic but not diffeomorphic to complex projective space; the explicit residue-class result concerns complex dimensions n≥4.
sections.unique_caveat: The conjecture that every n≥4 works remains open; density one and more than 92% residue coverage do not settle the remaining dimensions.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: It gives both an asymptotic density theorem and an explicit modular classification, and links smoothing theory to stable cohomotopy and chromatic homotopy theory.

sections.title: Conformal Bootstrap Unblocked
sections.abstract: The authors formulate a conformal-bootstrap hierarchy using reflection-positive Gram matrices, conformal symmetry, and crossing, without taking the operator product expansion or conformal blocks as inputs, and demonstrate bounds in one to three dimensions.
sections.claimed_result: The authors construct a hierarchy of semidefinite programs from Gram-matrix positivity and show that it yields correlator and spectral bounds, including the stated Ising features, without explicitly using conformal blocks (arXiv abstract and Sections 2–5).
sections.assumptions_and_setting: Conformal field theory constraints from conformal symmetry, reflection positivity, crossing, and any added spectral assumptions; demonstrations cover dimensions one through three.
sections.unique_caveat: The authors report rapidly growing Gram-matrix sizes and leave open whether the hierarchy becomes equivalent to the conventional conformal-block bootstrap at infinite truncation.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: It proposes a distinct mathematical-physics method and reports recovery of generalized-free-field behavior and characteristic two- and three-dimensional Ising kinks; the math-ph cross-list makes the archive inclusion explicit.

sections.title: Gradient higher integrability for a general class of degenerate parabolic double phase systems
sections.abstract: The authors prove local higher-integrability estimates for weak solutions of generalized double-phase parabolic systems, under structural conditions on the growth functions and the continuity modulus of the phase coefficient.
sections.claimed_result: For solutions in L∞(0,T;L^s), 2≤s<∞, the authors establish Ψ(·,|Du|)∈L^(1+ε)_loc for some ε>0 under their stated modulus-to-growth condition (arXiv abstract).
sections.assumptions_and_setting: Degenerate parabolic systems with Ψ(z,κ)=G(κ)+a(z)H(κ), Young functions G,H satisfying structural assumptions, nonnegative a with concave parabolic modulus ω, and the explicit limsup condition given in the abstract.
sections.unique_caveat: The higher-integrability conclusion is conditional on the growth and modulus hypotheses; it is not a general estimate for all degenerate parabolic systems.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: The result extends power-growth gap conditions to general Young-function growth and continuity moduli, with a 54-page argument combining intrinsic stopping times and reverse-Hölder estimates.

sections.title: Trending Research Themes
text: Discrepancy meets online sampling: the two Tusnády papers (2611.06998, 2611.08455) share the sharp fixed-dimensional order; Wengiel supplies the new d≥3 lower bound used with prior results, while Lei adds robust deletion and online thinning.

Sharp quantitative thresholds across models: void percolation (2611.07196) pins down linear-in-d scaling; the K3 classification (2611.08356) gives an exact finite-field cutoff. These are separate techniques.
Geometry translated into algebraic invariants: the K3 result uses zeta-function and lattice constraints; exotic smoothings of CP^n (2611.08406) use stable cohomotopy and chromatic homotopy.
The direct-positivity conformal-bootstrap method (2611.07004) is an isolated methodological signal, not evidence of a field-wide shift.
The stochastic heat result (2611.07310) and double-phase estimates (2611.08291) make progress under distinct, carefully stated hypotheses; no shared proof technique is claimed.

sections.title: Open Problems and Research Directions
text: Author-stated: online terminal-discrepancy bounds for k≥2 differ by log n in 2611.08455; close the factor or test whether it is necessary.
Synthesis: track dimension dependence in the fixed-dimension discrepancy constants of 2611.06998 and 2611.08455.
Synthesis: sharpen the d/2 to 5d void-percolation bounds or test whether Φ_p(d)/d converges (2611.07196).
Author-stated: reconcile the Artin–Tate/lattice argument in 2611.08356 with the other proof based on Frobenius actions.
Author-stated: settle whether every CP^n for n≥4 admits an exotic smoothing; remaining residue dimensions are a target for extending 2611.08406.
Author-stated: improve efficiency and determine infinite-truncation equivalence with the conformal-block bootstrap (2611.07004).
Author-stated: test whether the unbounded-diffusion theorem in 2611.07310 can use L² instead of L∞ initial data.

sections.title: Takeaway
sections.text: This batch’s clearest headline is mathematical sharpening: a long-standing discrepancy order is settled in higher dimensions, and a high-dimensional percolation threshold is shown to be linear. Alongside those are exact arithmetic-geometric classifications and method advances in stochastic PDE and conformal bootstrap; because attention metrics are sparse for such recent submissions, this ordering is evidence-informed notability, not measured popularity.
